title: Invariant registry
description: One area's invariant registry (design 6.3, the adversarial loop): the properties that must always hold, each in a form the adversarial pass can attack with generated inputs. It lives in the knowledge base at kb/areas/<area>/invariants.json, or where the area's invariants pointer in policy.json says. Plain data: it names exports of the area's own modules, which the pass calls in a separate process, and never a command.

area.description: The area in policy.json (rights.areas) this registry belongs to.

tests_dir.description: Where a break's regression test is written, repository-relative: a directory the area's test suite runs.

fix_parent.description: The project a break's fix item is filed under, unless the command names another.

id.description: Unique in the registry; names the regression tests of its breaks.

statement.description: The property in one sentence, as a person would say it.

checked.description: When a person last confirmed the invariant still states what matters (design 6.3, step 1).

form.description: How the pass attacks it. round-trip: inverse(target(x)) equals x. idempotent: target(target(x)) equals target(x). differential: target agrees with oracle. order-independent: reordering the first argument, a list, changes nothing. total: target never throws. holds: target is a property the area wrote, and returns true.

module.description: The module that exports target, repository-relative.

target.description: The export under attack (for holds, the property).

inverse.description: round-trip only: the export that undoes target.

oracle.description: differential only: the export target must agree with, such as a simple slow version or the previous implementation.

oracle_module.description: differential only: the oracle's module, when it is not module.

args.description: One generator per argument of target.

runs.description: How many argument lists the pass tries (default 300).

chars.description: The characters drawn from (default: printable ASCII).
